mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 3% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a more than 5% drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals a coordinated collapse in demand drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -3% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000, signals a sudden labor market deterioration, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change < -0.5pp AND PAYEMS monthly change < -100000
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase of more than 4% in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) for three consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts anticipatory monetary tightening and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
